To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of CD4+ cells in metastatic malignant tumours correlates with the therapeutic efficacy of IFN-alpha and may therefore be of prognostic value in patients with malignant melanoma.
the presence of CD4+ cells in fine needle aspirations of metastases is associated with a favourable outcome in patients with malignant melanoma treated with IFN-alpha.
patients with systemic malignant melanoma and a high number of tumour infiltrating CD4 lymphocytes have a favourable response to interferon treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a prognostic tool for the prediction of response to IFN-alpha in metastatic melanoma.

the possibility that the presence of tumour-inflitrating CD4+ cells in fine needle aspirations from metastatic lesions of malignant melanoma is an important prognostic factor for the response to IFN-alpha treatment.
the development of a simple and rapid technique that may be of use to identify patients likely to respond to IFN-alpha treatment in malignant melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

patients with systemic metastatic disease who have moderate to high numbers (greater than or equal to 10% of the cells) of infiltrating CD8+ and CD4+ cells have a significantly better response to IFN-alpha than patients with a low number (less than or equal to less than 10%) of such cells (P < 0001).
patients with systemic metastatic malignant melanomas who have high numbers of infiltrated CD4+ cells are likely to benefit from IFN-alpha therapy.
the presence of CD4+ T lymphocytes in fine-needle aspirates of malignant melanoma metastases correlates strongly with the response to treatment with IFN-alpha.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with a high number of infiltrating CD+ cells in fine needle biopsies are more likely to respond to IFN-alpha treatment than are those with a low number.
IFN-alpha treatment is more effective in patients with high numbers of tumour infiltrating CD4 lymphocytes.
patients with a high proportion of tumour-invasive CD4+ lymphocyte infiltration in fine needle aspirate specimens of metastatic malignant melanomas are likely to respond to IFN-alpha.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of infiltrating CD8+ and CD4+ lymphocyte subsets in metastatic lesions of malignant melanoma is a predictor of the therapeutic benefit from IFN-alpha.
the degree of CD4+ infiltration in tumour metastases correlates with response to IFN-alpha treatment in malignant melanoma.

patients with systemic metastatic malignant melanomas and a high number of infiltrating CD+ lymphocytes in metastases are more likely to benefit from IFN-alpha therapy than patients without this feature.
